job: Rework their text-to-SQL query tool so its default execution path is a parser-validated, SELECT-only allowlist with a dialect-aware dangerous-pattern blocklist.
outcome: A shipped framework release whose database-query tool defaults to read-only execution, treating write/DDL/program-execution SQL as explicit opt-in.
motivation: Avoid drawing their own CVSS-critical advisory once researchers replay the prompt-to-SQL-to-RCE pattern against their unguarded default.

task.who: core maintainers of the SQL/text-to-SQL tooling module
task.what: default the query tool to a SELECT-only allowlist
task.where: the framework's SQL execution wrapper in the upstream repo
task.why: make the wrapper the injection enforcement point
task.how: parser-based allowlist (e.g. sqlglot) plus pattern blocklist

job: Rewrite tool docs to elevate least-privilege, read-only database credentials from an optional footnote to a stated prerequisite alongside the new default guard.
outcome: Published documentation framing read-only DB credentials as a required deployment baseline rather than advisory best practice.
motivation: Reinforce the safe-by-default posture and reduce deployer misconfiguration that would still surface as framework-attributed incidents.

task.what: elevate least-privilege credentials to a stated prerequisite
task.where: the tool's official documentation and security guidance
task.when: alongside the guard release, through Q1 2027
task.why: harden the default posture against misconfiguration

job: Replay the prompt-injection-to-SQL-to-RCE pattern across additional agent frameworks and file CVSS-critical advisories against tools that keep write SQL on by default.
outcome: A stream of critical CVEs that makes opt-in-only hardening untenable and pressures maintainers to ship the read-only default.
motivation: Demonstrate that the framework's execution wrapper, not just the deployer's DB role, must be the enforcement point against model-authored SQL.

task.what: replay prompt-to-SQL-to-RCE exploits against agent frameworks
task.where: open-source agent libraries and their disclosure programs
task.why: prove the wrapper must enforce, not the DB role
task.how: prompt-injection exploit chains and CVSS advisories
